title: Overhaul short_answer.py grader with grading table, JSON output, and calibration
acceptance_criteria: New system prompt instructs the LLM to return a JSON object with an array of sub-question results, each containing: label, raw_score (0 to sub-question max), max_score, reasoning (<=200 chars), and feedback (<=300 chars)
User prompt includes: question description (truncated to 2000 chars), reference answer (truncated to 1000 chars), rubric, student answer (truncated to 2000 chars), and the grading_table JSON
LLM call uses profile='grading' with chat() helper (not raw max_tokens=16)
Response JSON is parsed; falls back to old single-case behavior on parse failure (lenient degradation)
Each sub-question score is calibrated via calibrate_score(raw_score, sub_max, strictness) from calibration.py
Per-sub-question SubmissionTestCase rows are created with: case=N, status=AC/WA, points=calibrated_score, total=sub_max, feedback=LLM feedback string, extended_feedback=LLM reasoning
When grading_table is None: falls back to legacy single-case 0-100 grading (preserves backward compatibility)
Implements retry logic: HTTP 429/500/502/503/504 → exponential backoff (1s, 5s, 25s), max 3 retries
All scores round to 0.5 precision before creating SubmissionTestCase
